anomalies.title: The exit monitor's strategy list has a registry-failure fallback that covers 0 of 52 routed-live legs
anomalies.measured: Parsed config/strategies.yaml (55 declared) and config/accounts.yaml (11 accounts) on the working tree at 0d3ab95, 2026-09-22. 52 distinct strategies are routed to at least one mode:live account. src/runtime/pipeline.py:349-351 returns the hardcoded fallback ['turtle_soup','vwap'] when load_strategies() raises. Neither name is routed to ANY live account: turtle_soup is execution:shadow, vwap is enabled:false + execution:shadow. Set difference: 52 of 52 routed-live legs absent from the fallback.
anomalies.why_it_matters: STRATEGIES is consumed by BOTH halves. Entry: the multiplexer would try 2 strategies that trade nothing. Exit: run_exit_evaluation_tick calls _load_strategies(None) -> pipeline.STRATEGIES, then get_order_packages_by_strategy per name -- so every open package belonging to the other 52 legs gets NO monitor() call: no trailing amend, no stale-exit, no giveback stop, no exit head. Open real-money positions would sit unmanaged until a broker-side bracket or the reconciler caught them.
anomalies.trigger_reachability: Not hypothetical. STRATEGIES is a module-level constant evaluated once at import; the fallback fires on any load_strategies() exception -- a malformed config/strategies.yaml being the live one. ict-git-sync pulls main every ~5 min, so a YAML syntax error landing on main reaches the live trader inside ~5 minutes.
anomalies.silence: It announces itself with ONE logger.warning at import. None of the health snapshot's 7 checks (service, git_drift, git_fetch, tick, accounts_api, db, disk) would go red: the process is alive, ticking, in sync and the DB answers. The snapshot would keep reading '7/7 checks ok'.
anomalies.field_beats_comment: The comment at src/runtime/pipeline.py:350 asserts 'hardcoded fallback matches the production roster in config/strategies.yaml after PR B1'. MEASURED today it matches 0 of 52. This is the same shape as the trainer flock comment fixed in de20550 -- prose describing a mechanism that no longer exists.
anomalies.second_collapse: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:124-126 -- _load_strategies returns [] on exception with a warning, and the tick then returns {} summaries. 'We could not resolve the strategy list' and 'no strategy had anything open' are indistinguishable downstream.
anomalies.proposed_fix: Tier-2, NOT applied by this review (the skill forbids touching src/ and this is runtime). (1) Delete the value fallback: on registry failure RAISE, or return a sentinel the callers must branch on -- a trader that cannot read its own roster must not silently run a two-name one. (2) Make the exit half's population open-package-driven (SELECT DISTINCT strategy FROM order_packages WHERE status='open') UNION the roster, so an open position is monitored on the strength of BEING OPEN, never on the strength of appearing in a list. (3) Add a health check 'STRATEGIES length vs strategies.yaml enabled count' so the divergence is loud.
anomalies.verification_note: A related hypothesis was checked and REFUTED, and is recorded so it is not re-derived: the TLT position open on alpaca_live (id 5924, pattern tlt_pullback_1h, opened 2026-09-18) belongs to a leg A6/#12673 removed from the alpaca_live ROSTER on 2026-09-21. It is NOT stranded -- exit evaluation iterates STRATEGIES (the strategies.yaml registry), not account rosters, and tlt_pullback_1h is still enabled:true/execution:live there. Its r-block updated 05:29Z. Roster removal does not strand an open position; registry FAILURE would strand all of them.

anomalies.title: The health snapshot reports 7/7 ok while structurally unable to see the failure that actually happened
anomalies.measured: /api/bot/health/latest read 2026-09-22T05:30Z, snapshot ts 05:16:31Z: status ok, summary '7/7 checks ok', action_required false. The 7 checks are service, git_drift, git_fetch, tick, accounts_api, db, disk. The accounts_api check's own detail reads: 'all 8 recorded broker-API accounts ok (1 manual-bridge skipped: breakout_1; 2 dry/shelved skipped: ib_live, oanda_practice)'.
anomalies.why_it_matters: breakout_1 is a FUNDED prop account that received zero tickets for three weeks (row E16, measured 21 of 21) and nobody noticed from the inside. The snapshot's account check EXCLUDES it by construction -- it is the one account skipped -- and there is no check anywhere in the 7 that asks whether signals, intents or tickets are still being produced. So the surface the operator looks at was green throughout the failure and would be green through the next one.
anomalies.cross_check: /api/bot/accounts/balances confirms breakout_1 balance:null, open_positions:null, api_ok:false. The data is honest (null, not 0 -- the repo's own rule followed correctly). The defect is that nothing GRADES it: an account that is permanently api_ok:false is indistinguishable from one that just went dark.
anomalies.relation_to_E18: COMPLEMENTS, does not duplicate. E18 is the missing detector (intents produced vs tickets the account actually received). This is narrower and cheaper: the EXISTING health snapshot counts a structurally-skipped account toward a 7/7 all-clear. E18 builds the missing measurement; this says the existing all-clear must stop claiming coverage it does not have.
anomalies.proposed_fix: Tier-1 where it lands in the snapshot generator's reporting (no runtime path): (a) report skipped accounts as a distinct state in the summary line -- '7/7 ok, 3 accounts NOT CHECKED' rather than folding them into ok; (b) add a liveness check keyed on last-ticket-age per routed account, which is the check whose absence E16 measured.

anomalies.title: The health-review skill's own completion gate points at a file the 2026-09-21 reset archived
anomalies.measured: .claude/skills/health-review/SKILL.md names docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json in five places, including the section headed 'Draining the backlog -- a HARD COMPLETION GATE (not a sample)' and the Output contract's backlog_coverage.count_untriaged == 0 requirement. `ls docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json` -> No such file or directory. It is archived under docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/.
anomalies.why_it_matters: The skill's hard completion gate is unsatisfiable, so EVERY health-review from the reset onward is either incomplete by its own contract or quietly ignores its own gate. The skill also still anchors its review WINDOW on that file's newest backlog_drain timestamp, so the window has no anchor either. A binding skill (instruction-hierarchy level 5) instructing something that cannot be done is the same defect class the canonical rules record at 'THIS RULE NAMED FIVE OTHER WORDS UNTIL 2026-09-12'.
anomalies.also: comms/schema/health_review_response.template.json's findings status enum is `ok | watch | concern` with no value for 'we did not look'. Under a diag outage the template forces an unmeasurable dimension to be rendered as a measurement outcome. This review emitted `could_not_look` rather than comply.
anomalies.proposed_fix: Tier-1. Re-point the skill's backlog sections at docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl + MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, re-anchor the window on the newest health review under comms/reviews/health/, and add `could_not_look` to the template's status enum (registering the three-way contract with collapsed-state-guard's CONTRACTS table is the mechanical form).

anomalies.title: This review could not produce the MANDATORY security stated-negative
anomalies.measured: 0 of 5 declared breach-sweep sources were swept. Host auth signals are blocked behind /api/diag/* (3/3 401). The four GitHub-side sources were not run within this lane's budget.
anomalies.why_it_matters: The skill is explicit that a clean security check must be a stated verification and that an empty security finding is a review failure. This review therefore does NOT state one. Recorded so the gap is visible rather than absorbed.
